q: The smallest unit of biological structure that meets the functional requirements of “living” is the ________.
why: The correct answer is: cell. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following sequences represents the hierarchy of biological organization from the most complex to the least complex level?
options: organism, community, biosphere, molecule, tissue, organ
why: The correct answer is: biosphere, ecosystem, community, population, organism. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “a basic unit of matter that cannot be broken down by normal chemical reactions”
why: atom: a basic unit of matter that cannot be broken down by normal chemical reactions

q: Which term matches this definition? “a collection of all ecosystems on Earth”
why: biosphere: a collection of all ecosystems on Earth

q: Which term matches this definition? “the smallest fundamental unit of structure and function in living things”
why: cell: the smallest fundamental unit of structure and function in living things

q: Which term matches this definition? “a set of populations inhabiting a particular area”
why: community: a set of populations inhabiting a particular area

q: Which term matches this definition? “all living things in a particular area together with the abiotic, nonliving parts of that environment”
why: ecosystem: all living things in a particular area together with the abiotic, nonliving parts of that environment

q: Which term matches this definition? “an organism with cells that have nuclei and membrane-bound organelles”
why: eukaryote: an organism with cells that have nuclei and membrane-bound organelles

card.q: Using examples, explain how biology can be studied from a microscopic approach to a global approach.
card.a: Researchers can approach biology from the smallest to the largest, and everything in between. For instance, an ecologist may study a population of individuals, the population’s community, the community’s ecosystem, and the ecosystem’s part in the biosphere. When studying an individual organism, a biologist could examine the cell and its organelles, the tissues that the cells make up, the organs and their respective organ systems, and the sum total—the organism itself.

q: A suggested and testable explanation for an event is called a ________.
why: The correct answer is: hypothesis. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The type of logical thinking that uses related observations to arrive at a general conclusion is called ________.
why: The correct answer is: inductive reasoning. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “a form of science that solves real-world problems”
why: applied science: a form of science that solves real-world problems

q: Which term matches this definition? “science that seeks to expand knowledge regardless of the short-term application of that knowledge”
why: basic science: science that seeks to expand knowledge regardless of the short-term application of that knowledge

q: Which term matches this definition? “a part of an experiment that does not change during the experiment”
why: control: a part of an experiment that does not change during the experiment

q: Which term matches this definition? “a form of logical thinking that uses a general statement to predict specific results”
why: deductive reasoning: a form of logical thinking that uses a general statement to predict specific results

q: Which term matches this definition? “a form of science that aims to observe, explore, and find things out”
why: descriptive science: a form of science that aims to observe, explore, and find things out

q: Which term matches this definition? “able to be disproven by experimental results”
why: falsifiable: able to be disproven by experimental results

card.q: Give an example of how applied science has had a direct effect on your daily life.
card.a: s will vary. One example of how applied science has had a direct effect on daily life is the presence of vaccines. Vaccines to prevent diseases such polio, measles, tetanus, and even the influenza affect daily life by contributing to individual and societal health.

q: Magnesium has an atomic number of 12. Which of the following statements is true of a neutral magnesium atom?
options: It has 12 protons, 12 electrons, and 12 neutrons.
It has 12 protons, 12 electrons, and six neutrons.
It has six protons, six electrons, and no neutrons.
It has six protons, six electrons, and six neutrons.
why: The correct answer is: It has 12 protons, 12 electrons, and 12 neutrons.. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which type of bond represents a weak chemical bond?
why: The correct answer is: hydrogen bond. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: An isotope of sodium (Na) has a mass number of 22. How many neutrons does it have?
why: The correct answer is: 11. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “a negative ion formed by gaining electrons”
why: anion: a negative ion formed by gaining electrons

q: Which term matches this definition? “the number of protons in an atom”
why: atomic number: the number of protons in an atom

q: Which term matches this definition? “a positive ion formed by losing electrons”
why: cation: a positive ion formed by losing electrons

q: Which term matches this definition? “an interaction between two or more of the same or different elements that results in the formation of molecules”
why: chemical bond: an interaction between two or more of the same or different elements that results in the formation of molecules

q: Which term matches this definition? “a type of strong bond between two or more of the same or different elements; forms when electrons are shared between elements”
why: covalent bond: a type of strong bond between two or more of the same or different elements; forms when electrons are shared between elements

q: Which term matches this definition? “a negatively charged particle that resides outside of the nucleus in the electron orbital; lacks functional mass and has a charge of –1”
why: electron: a negatively charged particle that resides outside of the nucleus in the electron orbital; lacks functional mass and has a charge of –1

card.q: How many neutrons do (K) potassium-39 and potassium-40 have, respectively?
card.a: Potassium-39 has twenty neutrons. Potassium-40 has twenty one neutrons.

card.q: Why are hydrogen bonds and van der Waals interactions necessary for cells?
card.a: Hydrogen bonds and van der Waals interactions form weak associations between different molecules. They provide the structure and shape necessary for proteins and DNA within cells so that they function properly. Hydrogen bonds also give water its unique properties, which are necessary for life.

q: Which of the following statements is not true?
options: Water is the most abundant molecule in Earth’s atmosphere.
why: The correct answer is: Water is the most abundant molecule in Earth’s atmosphere.. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Using a pH meter, you find the pH of an unknown solution to be 8.0. How would you describe this solution?
why: The correct answer is: weakly basic. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The pH of lemon juice is about 2.0, whereas tomato juice's pH is about 4.0. Approximately how much of an increase in hydrogen ion concentration is there between tomato juice and lemon juice?
why: The correct answer is: 100 times. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “a substance that donates hydrogen ions and therefore lowers pH”
why: acid: a substance that donates hydrogen ions and therefore lowers pH

q: Which term matches this definition? “the attraction between water molecules and molecules of a different substance”
why: adhesion: the attraction between water molecules and molecules of a different substance

q: Which term matches this definition? “a substance that absorbs hydrogen ions and therefore raises pH”
why: base: a substance that absorbs hydrogen ions and therefore raises pH

q: Which term matches this definition? “a solution that resists a change in pH by absorbing or releasing hydrogen or hydroxide ions”
why: buffer: a solution that resists a change in pH by absorbing or releasing hydrogen or hydroxide ions

q: Which term matches this definition? “the intermolecular forces between water molecules caused by the polar nature of water; creates surface tension”
why: cohesion: the intermolecular forces between water molecules caused by the polar nature of water; creates surface tension

q: Which term matches this definition? “the release of water molecules from liquid water to form water vapor”
why: evaporation: the release of water molecules from liquid water to form water vapor

card.q: Why can some insects walk on water?
card.a: Some insects can walk on water, although they are heavier (denser) than water, because of the surface tension of water. Surface tension results from cohesion, or the attraction between water molecules at the surface of the body of water [the liquid-air (gas) interface].

card.q: Explain why water is an excellent solvent.
card.a: Water molecules are polar, meaning they have separated partial positive and negative charges. Because of these charges, water molecules are able to surround charged particles created when a substance dissociates. The surrounding layer of water molecules stabilizes the ion and keeps differently charged ions from reassociating, so the substance stays dissolved.

q: An example of a monosaccharide is ________.
why: The correct answer is: all of the above. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Cellulose and starch are examples of ________.
why: The correct answer is: polysaccharides. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Phospholipids are important components of __________.
options: the plasma membrane of animal cells
the double bond in hydrocarbon chains
why: The correct answer is: the plasma membrane of animal cells. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The monomers that make up proteins are called _________.
why: The correct answer is: amino acids. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “a monomer of a protein”
why: amino acid: a monomer of a protein

q: Which term matches this definition? “a biological macromolecule in which the ratio of carbon to hydrogen to oxygen is 1:2:1; carbohydrates serve as energy sources and structural support in cells”
why: carbohydrate: a biological macromolecule in which the ratio of carbon to hydrogen to oxygen is 1:2:1; carbohydrates serve as energy sources and structural support in cells

q: Which term matches this definition? “a polysaccharide that makes up the cell walls of plants and provides structural support to the cell”
why: cellulose: a polysaccharide that makes up the cell walls of plants and provides structural support to the cell

q: Which term matches this definition? “a type of carbohydrate that forms the outer skeleton of arthropods, such as insects and crustaceans, and the cell walls of fungi”
why: chitin: a type of carbohydrate that forms the outer skeleton of arthropods, such as insects and crustaceans, and the cell walls of fungi

q: Which term matches this definition? “the loss of shape in a protein as a result of changes in temperature, pH, or exposure to chemicals”
why: denaturation: the loss of shape in a protein as a result of changes in temperature, pH, or exposure to chemicals

q: Which term matches this definition? “a double-stranded polymer of nucleotides that carries the hereditary information of the cell”
why: deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA): a double-stranded polymer of nucleotides that carries the hereditary information of the cell

card.q: Explain at least three functions that lipids serve in plants and/or animals.
card.a: Fat serves as a valuable way for animals to store energy. It can also provide insulation. Phospholipids and steroids are important components of cell membranes.

card.q: Explain what happens if even one amino acid is substituted for another in a polypeptide chain. Provide a specific example.
card.a: A change in gene sequence can lead to a different amino acid being added to a polypeptide chain instead of the normal one. This causes a change in protein structure and function. For example, in sickle cell anemia, the hemoglobin β chain has a single amino acid substitution. Because of this change, the disc-shaped red blood cells assume a crescent shape, which can result in serious health problems.

q: When viewing a specimen through a light microscope, scientists use _________ to distinguish the individual components of cells.
why: The correct answer is: special stains. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The ___________ is the basic unit of life.
why: The correct answer is: cell. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “the instrument that magnifies an object”
why: microscope: the instrument that magnifies an object

q: Which term matches this definition? “the biological concept that states that all organisms are composed of one or more cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and new cells arise from existing cells”
why: unified cell theory: the biological concept that states that all organisms are composed of one or more cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and new cells arise from existing cells

card.q: What are the advantages and disadvantages of light, transmission, and scanning electron microscopes?
card.a: The advantages of light microscopes are that they are easily obtained, and the light beam does not kill the cells. However, typical light microscopes are somewhat limited in the amount of detail that they can reveal. Electron microscopes are ideal because you can view intricate details, but they are bulky and costly, and preparation for the microscopic examination kills the specimen. Transmission electron microscopes are designed to examine the internal structures of a cell, whereas a scanning electron microscope only allows visualization of the surface of a structure.

q: Which of these do all prokaryotes and eukaryotes share?
why: The correct answer is: plasma membrane. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: A typical prokaryotic cell __________________ compared to a eukaryotic cell.
options: is smaller in size by a factor of 100
is smaller in size by a factor of one million
is larger in size by a factor of 10
why: The correct answer is: is smaller in size by a factor of 100. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “a cell that has a membrane-bound nucleus and several other membrane-bound compartments or sacs”
why: eukaryotic cell: a cell that has a membrane-bound nucleus and several other membrane-bound compartments or sacs

q: Which term matches this definition? “a membrane-bound compartment or sac within a cell”
why: organelle: a membrane-bound compartment or sac within a cell

q: Which term matches this definition? “a unicellular organism that lacks a nucleus or any other membrane-bound organelle”
why: prokaryotic cell: a unicellular organism that lacks a nucleus or any other membrane-bound organelle

card.q: Describe the structures that are characteristic of a prokaryote cell.
card.a: Prokaryotic cells are surrounded by a plasma membrane and have DNA, cytoplasm, and ribosomes, like eukaryotic cells. They also have cell walls and may have a cell capsule. Prokaryotes have a single large chromosome that is not surrounded by a nuclear membrane. Prokaryotes may have flagella or motility, pili for conjugation, and fimbriae for adhesion to surfaces.

q: Which of the following is found both in eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells?
why: The correct answer is: ribosome. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following is not a component of the endomembrane system?
why: The correct answer is: mitochondrion. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “a rigid cell covering made of cellulose in plants, peptidoglycan in bacteria, non-peptidoglycan compounds in Archaea, and chitin in fungi that protects the cell, provides structural support, and gives shape to the cell”
why: cell wall: a rigid cell covering made of cellulose in plants, peptidoglycan in bacteria, non-peptidoglycan compounds in Archaea, and chitin in fungi that protects the cell, provides structural support, and gives shape to the cell

q: Which term matches this definition? “a large plant cell organelle that acts as a storage compartment, water reservoir, and site of macromolecule degradation”
why: central vacuole: a large plant cell organelle that acts as a storage compartment, water reservoir, and site of macromolecule degradation

q: Which term matches this definition? “a plant cell organelle that carries out photosynthesis”
why: chloroplast: a plant cell organelle that carries out photosynthesis

q: Which term matches this definition? “protein-DNA complex that serves as the chromosomes' building material”
why: chromatin: protein-DNA complex that serves as the chromosomes' building material

q: Which term matches this definition? “structure within the nucleus that comprises chromatin that contains DNA, the hereditary material”
why: chromosome: structure within the nucleus that comprises chromatin that contains DNA, the hereditary material

q: Which term matches this definition? “(plural: cilia) a short, hair-like structure that extends from the plasma membrane in large numbers and is used to move an entire cell or move substances along the outer surface of the cell”
why: cilium: (plural: cilia) a short, hair-like structure that extends from the plasma membrane in large numbers and is used to move an entire cell or move substances along the outer surface of the cell

card.q: What structures does a plant cell have that an animal cell does not have? What structures does an animal cell have that a plant cell does not have?
card.a: Plant cells have plasmodesmata, a cell wall, a large central vacuole, chloroplasts, and plastids. Animal cells have lysosomes and centrosomes.

card.q: Why does the cis face of the Golgi not face the plasma membrane?
card.a: Because that face receives chemicals from the ER, which is toward the center of the cell.

card.q: In the context of cell biology, what do we mean by form follows function? What are at least two examples of this concept?
card.a: “Form follows function” refers to the idea that the function of a body part dictates the form of that body part. As an example, organisms like birds or fish that fly or swim quickly through the air or water have streamlined bodies that reduce drag. At the level of the cell, in tissues involved in secretory functions, such as the salivary glands, the cells have abundant Golgi.

q: Which plasma membrane component can be either found on its surface or embedded in the membrane structure?
why: The correct answer is: protein. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The tails of the phospholipids of the plasma membrane are composed of _____ and are _______?
why: The correct answer is: fatty acid groups; hydrophobic. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “a model of the structure of the plasma membrane as a mosaic of components, including phospholipids, cholesterol, proteins, and glycolipids, resulting in a fluid rather than static character”
why: fluid mosaic model: a model of the structure of the plasma membrane as a mosaic of components, including phospholipids, cholesterol, proteins, and glycolipids, resulting in a fluid rather than static character

card.q: Why is it advantageous for the cell membrane to be fluid in nature?
card.a: The fluidity of the cell membrane is necessary for the operation of some enzymes and transport mechanisms within the membrane.

q: Water moves via osmosis _________.
options: from an area with a high concentration of other solutes to a lower one
from an area with a low concentration of solutes to an area with a higher one
from an area with a low concentration of water to one of higher concentration
why: The correct answer is: from an area with a low concentration of solutes to an area with a higher one. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “an area of high concentration across from an area of low concentration”
why: concentration gradient: an area of high concentration across from an area of low concentration

q: Which term matches this definition? “a passive process of transport of low-molecular weight material down its concentration gradient”
why: diffusion: a passive process of transport of low-molecular weight material down its concentration gradient

q: Which term matches this definition? “a process by which material moves down a concentration gradient (from high to low concentration) using integral membrane proteins”
why: facilitated transport: a process by which material moves down a concentration gradient (from high to low concentration) using integral membrane proteins

q: Which term matches this definition? “describes a solution in which extracellular fluid has higher osmolarity than the fluid inside the cell”
why: hypertonic: describes a solution in which extracellular fluid has higher osmolarity than the fluid inside the cell

q: Which term matches this definition? “describes a solution in which extracellular fluid has lower osmolarity than the fluid inside the cell”
why: hypotonic: describes a solution in which extracellular fluid has lower osmolarity than the fluid inside the cell

q: Which term matches this definition? “describes a solution in which the extracellular fluid has the same osmolarity as the fluid inside the cell”
why: isotonic: describes a solution in which the extracellular fluid has the same osmolarity as the fluid inside the cell

card.q: A doctor injects a patient with what he thinks is isotonic saline solution. The patient dies, and autopsy reveals that many red blood cells have been destroyed. Do you think the solution the doctor injected was really isotonic?
card.a: No, it must have been hypotonic, as a hypotonic solution would cause water to enter the cells, thereby making them burst.

card.q: Why does osmosis occur?
card.a: Water moves through a semipermeable membrane in osmosis because there is a concentration gradient across the membrane of solute and solvent. The solute cannot effectively move to balance the concentration on both sides of the membrane, so water moves to achieve this balance.

q: Active transport must function continuously because __________.
options: cells must be in constant motion
diffusion is constantly moving the solutes in the other direction
why: The correct answer is: diffusion is constantly moving the solutes in the other direction. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “the method of transporting material that requires energy”
why: active transport: the method of transporting material that requires energy

q: Which term matches this definition? “a gradient produced by the combined forces of the electrical gradient and the chemical gradient”
why: electrochemical gradient: a gradient produced by the combined forces of the electrical gradient and the chemical gradient

q: Which term matches this definition? “a type of active transport that moves substances, including fluids and particles, into a cell”
why: endocytosis: a type of active transport that moves substances, including fluids and particles, into a cell

q: Which term matches this definition? “a process of passing material out of a cell”
why: exocytosis: a process of passing material out of a cell

q: Which term matches this definition? “a process that takes particulate matter like macromolecules, cells, or cell fragments that the cell needs from the extracellular fluid; a variation of endocytosis”
why: phagocytosis: a process that takes particulate matter like macromolecules, cells, or cell fragments that the cell needs from the extracellular fluid; a variation of endocytosis

q: Which term matches this definition? “a process that takes solutes that the cell needs from the extracellular fluid; a variation of endocytosis”
why: pinocytosis: a process that takes solutes that the cell needs from the extracellular fluid; a variation of endocytosis

card.q: Where does the cell get energy for active transport processes?
card.a: The cell harvests energy from ATP produced by its own metabolism to power active transport processes, such as pumps.

q: Which of the following is not an example of an energy transformation?
options: Heating up dinner in a microwave
why: The correct answer is: None of the above. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following is not true about enzymes?
options: They are consumed by the reactions they catalyze.
They are usually made of amino acids.
They lower the activation energy of chemical reactions.
Each one is specific to the particular substrate(s) to which it binds.
why: The correct answer is: They are consumed by the reactions they catalyze.. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “the amount of initial energy necessary for reactions to occur”
why: activation energy: the amount of initial energy necessary for reactions to occur

q: Which term matches this definition? “a specific region on the enzyme where the substrate binds”
why: active site: a specific region on the enzyme where the substrate binds

q: Which term matches this definition? “the mechanism for inhibiting enzyme action in which a regulatory molecule binds to a second site (not the active site) and initiates a conformation change in the active site, preventing binding with the substrate”
why: allosteric inhibition: the mechanism for inhibiting enzyme action in which a regulatory molecule binds to a second site (not the active site) and initiates a conformation change in the active site, preventing binding with the substrate

q: Which term matches this definition? “describes the pathway that requires a net energy input to synthesize complex molecules from simpler ones”
why: anabolic: describes the pathway that requires a net energy input to synthesize complex molecules from simpler ones

q: Which term matches this definition? “the concept of energy flow through living systems”
why: bioenergetics: the concept of energy flow through living systems

q: Which term matches this definition? “describes the pathway in which complex molecules are broken down into simpler ones, yielding energy as an additional product of the reaction”
why: catabolic: describes the pathway in which complex molecules are broken down into simpler ones, yielding energy as an additional product of the reaction

card.q: Look at each of the processes shown and decide if it is endergonic or exergonic.
card.a: A compost pile decomposing is an exergonic process. A baby developing from a fertilized egg is an endergonic process. Tea dissolving into water is an exergonic process. A ball rolling downhill is an exergonic process.

card.q: Does physical exercise to increase muscle mass involve anabolic and/or catabolic processes? Give evidence for your answer.
card.a: Physical exercise involves both anabolic and catabolic processes. Body cells break down sugars to provide ATP to do the work necessary for exercise, such as muscle contractions. This is catabolism. Muscle cells also must repair muscle tissue damaged by exercise by building new muscle. This is anabolism.

card.q: Explain in your own terms the difference between a spontaneous reaction and one that occurs instantaneously, and what causes this difference.
card.a: A spontaneous reaction is one that has a negative ∆G and thus releases energy. However, a spontaneous reaction need not occur quickly or suddenly like an instantaneous reaction. It may occur over long periods of time due to a large energy of activation, which prevents the reaction from occurring quickly.

card.q: With regard to enzymes, why are vitamins and minerals necessary for good health? Give examples.
card.a: Most vitamins and minerals act as cofactors and coenzymes for enzyme action. Many enzymes require the binding of certain cofactors or coenzymes to be able to catalyze their reactions. Since enzymes catalyze many important reactions, it is critical to obtain sufficient vitamins and minerals from diet and supplements. Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a coenzyme necessary for the action of enzymes that build collagen.

q: Energy is stored long-term in the bonds of _____ and used short-term to perform work from a(n) _____ molecule.
why: The correct answer is: glucose: ATP. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The energy currency used by cells is _____.
why: The correct answer is: ATP. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The glucose that enters the glycolysis pathway is split into two molecules of _________.
why: The correct answer is: pyruvate. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “(also, adenosine triphosphate) the cell’s energy currency”
why: ATP: (also, adenosine triphosphate) the cell’s energy currency

q: Which term matches this definition? “the process of breaking glucose into two three-carbon molecules with the production of ATP and NADH”
why: glycolysis: the process of breaking glucose into two three-carbon molecules with the production of ATP and NADH

card.q: Both prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms carry out some form of glycolysis. How does that fact support or not support the assertion that glycolysis is one of the oldest metabolic pathways?
card.a: If glycolysis evolved relatively late, it likely would not be as universal in organisms as it is. It probably evolved in very primitive organisms and persisted, with the addition of other pathways of carbohydrate metabolism that evolved later.

q: What do the electrons added to NAD⁺ do?
options: They become part of a fermentation pathway.
They go to another pathway for ATP production.
They energize the entry of the acetyl group into the citric acid cycle.
why: The correct answer is: They go to another pathway for ATP production.. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Chemiosmosis involves
options: the movement of electrons across the cell membrane
the movement of hydrogen atoms across a mitochondrial membrane
the movement of hydrogen ions across a mitochondrial membrane
the movement of glucose through the cell membrane
why: The correct answer is: the movement of hydrogen ions across a mitochondrial membrane. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “the combination of an acetyl group derived from pyruvic acid and coenzyme A which is made from pantothenic acid (a B-group vitamin)”
why: acetyl CoA: the combination of an acetyl group derived from pyruvic acid and coenzyme A which is made from pantothenic acid (a B-group vitamin)

q: Which term matches this definition? “a membrane-embedded protein complex that regenerates ATP from ADP with energy from protons diffusing through it”
why: ATP synthase: a membrane-embedded protein complex that regenerates ATP from ADP with energy from protons diffusing through it

q: Which term matches this definition? “the movement of hydrogen ions down their electrochemical gradient across a membrane through ATP synthase to generate ATP”
why: chemiosmosis: the movement of hydrogen ions down their electrochemical gradient across a membrane through ATP synthase to generate ATP

q: Which term matches this definition? “the production of ATP by the transfer of electrons down the electron transport chain to create a proton gradient that is used by ATP synthase to add phosphate groups to ADP molecules”
why: oxidative phosphorylation: the production of ATP by the transfer of electrons down the electron transport chain to create a proton gradient that is used by ATP synthase to add phosphate groups to ADP molecules

card.q: Cyanide inhibits cytochrome c oxidase, a component of the electron transport chain. If cyanide poisoning occurs, would you expect the pH of the intermembrane space to increase or decrease? What effect would cyanide have on ATP synthesis?
card.a: After cyanide poisoning, the electron transport chain can no longer pump electrons into the intermembrane space. The pH of the intermembrane space would increase, and ATP synthesis would stop.

card.q: We inhale oxygen when we breathe and exhale carbon dioxide. What is the oxygen used for and where does the carbon dioxide come from?
card.a: The oxygen we inhale is the final electron acceptor in the electron transport chain and allows aerobic respiration to proceed, which is the most efficient pathway for harvesting energy in the form of ATP from food molecules. The carbon dioxide we breathe out is formed during the citric acid cycle when the bonds in carbon compounds are broken.

q: Which of the following fermentation methods can occur in animal skeletal muscles?
why: The correct answer is: lactic acid fermentation. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “the use of an electron acceptor other than oxygen to complete metabolism using electron transport-based chemiosmosis”
why: anaerobic cellular respiration: the use of an electron acceptor other than oxygen to complete metabolism using electron transport-based chemiosmosis

q: Which term matches this definition? “the steps that follow the partial oxidation of glucose via glycolysis to regenerate NAD⁺; occurs in the absence of oxygen and uses an organic compound as the final electron acceptor”
why: fermentation: the steps that follow the partial oxidation of glucose via glycolysis to regenerate NAD⁺; occurs in the absence of oxygen and uses an organic compound as the final electron acceptor

card.q: Tremetol, a metabolic poison found in white snake root plant, prevents the metabolism of lactate. When cows eat this plant, Tremetol is concentrated in the milk. Humans who consume the milk become ill. Symptoms of this disease, which include vomiting, abdominal pain, and tremors, become worse after exercise. Why do you think this is the case?
card.a: The illness is caused by lactic acid build-up. Lactic acid levels rise after exercise, making the symptoms worse. Milk sickness is rare today, but was common in the Midwestern United States in the early 1800s.

card.q: When muscle cells run out of oxygen, what happens to the potential for energy extraction from sugars and what pathways do the cell use?
card.a: Without oxygen, oxidative phosphorylation and the citric acid cycle stop, so ATP is no longer generated through this mechanism, which extracts the greatest amount of energy from a sugar molecule. In addition, NADH accumulates, preventing glycolysis from going forward because of an absence of NAD⁺. Lactic acid fermentation uses the electrons in NADH to generate lactic acid from pyruvate, which allows glycolysis to continue and thus a smaller amount of ATP can be generated by the cell.

q: The cholesterol synthesized by cells uses which component of the glycolytic pathway as a starting point?
why: The correct answer is: acetyl CoA. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Beta oxidation is ________.
options: the removal of amino groups from amino acids
why: The correct answer is: the breakdown of fatty acids. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

card.q: Would you describe metabolic pathways as inherently wasteful or inherently economical, and why?
card.a: They are very economical. The substrates, intermediates, and products move between pathways and do so in response to finely tuned feedback inhibition loops that keep metabolism overall on an even keel. Intermediates in one pathway may occur in another, and they can move from one pathway to another fluidly in response to the needs of the cell.

q: What two products result from photosynthesis?
why: The correct answer is: glucose and oxygen. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which statement about thylakoids in eukaryotes is not correct?
options: Thylakoids exist as a maze of folded membranes.

card.q: Describe the pathway of energy in light-dependent reactions.

The energy of the electrochemical gradient is used to power ATP synthase, and the energy is transferred into a bond in the ATP molecule. In addition, energy from another photon can be used to create a high-energy bond in the molecule NADPH.

card.q: Describe the similarities and differences between the cytokinesis mechanisms found in animal cells versus those in plant cells.
card.a: There are very few similarities between animal cell and plant cell cytokinesis. In animal cells, a ring of actin fibers is formed around the periphery of the cell at the former metaphase plate. The actin ring contracts inward, pulling the plasma membrane toward the center of the cell until the cell is pinched in two. In plant cells, a new cell wall must be formed between the daughter cells. Because of the rigid cell walls of the parent cell, contraction of the middle of the cell is not possible. Instead, a cell plate is formed in the center of the cell at the former metaphase plate. The cell plate is formed from Golgi vesicles that contain enzymes, proteins, and glucose. The vesicles fuse and the enzymes build a new cell wall from the proteins and glucose. The cell plate grows toward, and eventually fuses with, the cell wall of the parent cell.

A tumor suppressor gene is a segment of DNA that codes for one of the negative cell-cycle regulators. If that gene becomes mutated to a form that is underactive, the cell cycle will run unchecked.

card.q: Explain the advantage that populations of sexually reproducing organisms have over asexually reproducing organisms?

In addition, the rate of adaptation of sexually reproducing organisms is higher, because of their increased variation. This may allow sexually reproducing organisms to adapt more quickly to competitors and parasites, who are evolving new ways to exploit or outcompete them.

card.q: Explain how the random alignment of homologous chromosomes during metaphase I contributes to variation in gametes produced by meiosis.
card.a: Random alignment leads to new combinations of traits. The chromosomes that were originally inherited by the gamete-producing individual came equally from the egg and the sperm. In metaphase I, the duplicated copies of these maternal and paternal homologous chromosomes line up across the center of the cell to form a tetrad. The orientation of each tetrad is random. There is an equal chance that the maternally derived chromosomes will be facing either pole. The same is true of the paternally derived chromosomes. The alignment should occur differently in almost every meiosis. As the homologous chromosomes are pulled apart in anaphase I, any combination of maternal and paternal chromosomes will move toward each pole. The gametes formed from these two groups of chromosomes will have a mixture of traits from the individual’s parents. Each gamete is unique.

card.q: In what ways is meiosis II similar to and different from mitosis of a diploid cell?
card.a: The two divisions are similar in that the chromosomes line up along the metaphase plate individually, meaning unpaired with other chromosomes (as in meiosis I). In addition, each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids that will be pulled apart. The two divisions are different because in meiosis II there are half the number of chromosomes that are present in a diploid cell of the same species undergoing mitosis. This is because meiosis I reduced the number of chromosomes to a haploid state.

card.q: Individuals with trisomy 21 are more likely to survive to adulthood than individuals with trisomy 18. Based on what you know about aneuploidies from this module, what can you hypothesize about chromosomes 21 and 18?
card.a: The problems caused by trisomies arise because the genes on the chromosome that is present in three copies produce more product than genes on chromosomes with only two copies. The cell does not have a way to adjust the amount of product, and the lack of balance causes problems in development and the maintenance of the individual. Each chromosome is different, and the differences in survivability could have to do with the numbers of genes on the two chromosomes. Chromosome 21 may be a smaller chromosome, so there are fewer unbalanced gene products. It is also possible that chromosome 21 carries genes whose products are less sensitive to differences in dosage than chromosome 18. The genes may be less involved in critical pathways, or the differences in dosage may make less of a difference to those pathways.

card.q: Use a Punnett square to predict the offspring in a cross between a dwarf pea plant (homozygous recessive) and a tall pea plant (heterozygous). What is the phenotypic ratio of the offspring?
